title: Numerals 6: Collective Numbers (двое, трое, четверо)
description: Collective numerals двое, трое, четверо count people as a group and pair with paired or plural-only nouns. They take the genitive plural: двое детей, трое друзей, четверо суток.
descriptionRussian: Собирательные числительные двое, трое, четверо считают людей как группу и сочетаются с парными существительными и существительными только во множественном числе. После них — родительный падеж множественного числа: двое детей, трое друзей, четверо суток.
intro: Russian has a second set of low numbers used for groups of people, and they take a different noun form from the ordinary ones. Two friends can be said two ways, and the collective version is the more natural one for a group. They are also compulsory with plural-only nouns, because ordinary numbers cannot attach to those at all.
rules: Collective numerals двое, трое, четверо count a GROUP. Use them with people (двое друзей), with children (двое детей), and with paired or plural-only nouns (двое суток, трое ножниц).
After a collective numeral the noun is in the GENITIVE PLURAL, the same ending you use after пять: двое детей, трое друзей, четверо студентов.
This differs from the ordinary numbers: два друга (genitive singular) vs двое друзей (genitive plural). Same meaning 'two friends', different grammar.
Collectives are normal with masculine and mixed groups and with дети. For an all-female group Russian usually prefers the ordinary number: две подруги, not двое подруг.
For plural-only nouns (сутки, ножницы, очки) collectives are required, because the ordinary numbers cannot attach: двое суток, not два суток.
examples: У Лены двое детей. (Lena has two children.) двое + genitive plural детей.
Трое друзей пошли в кино. (Three friends went to the cinema.) трое + genitive plural друзей.
В команде четверо студентов. (There are four students on the team.) четверо + genitive plural студентов.
Мы ехали туда двое суток. (We travelled there for two full days.) сутки is plural-only, so двое суток.
На столе лежат трое ножниц. (Three pairs of scissors lie on the table.) ножницы is plural-only: трое ножниц.
Сравни: два друга и двое друзей. (Compare: two friends and two friends.) genitive singular vs genitive plural.

items.hint: Counting children is the classic collective-numeral case.
items.explanation: Counting children uses the collective numeral двое, followed by the genitive plural: двое детей. This is the standard everyday phrase.

items.promptEnglish: Two friends went to the cinema.
items.hint: After a collective numeral, which case is the noun in?
items.explanation: Collective numerals take the genitive PLURAL, so двое друзей: the same ending you use after пять (пять друзей).

items.promptEnglish: We travelled there for two full days.
items.hint: Сутки is a plural-only noun, so the ordinary 'два' cannot attach.
items.explanation: Сутки ('a 24-hour day') exists only in the plural, so you cannot say два суток. The collective numeral steps in: двое суток.

items.promptEnglish: There are four students on the team.
items.hint: Counting a group of people (students) invites the collective form.
items.explanation: For a group of people, the collective numeral четверо is natural: четверо студентов, with the genitive plural. Четверо emphasises the group.

items.promptEnglish: Three pairs of scissors lie on the table.
items.hint: Collective + genitive plural; ножницы is plural-only.
items.explanation: Ножницы is plural-only, so it is counted with a collective numeral plus the genitive plural: трое ножниц. The genitive plural of ножницы is ножниц.

items.promptEnglish: Compare: two friends (ordinary) and two friends (collective).
items.hint: The second phrase needs the collective partner of два.
items.explanation: The collective counterpart of два is двое. Note the noun also shifts: два друга (gen.Sing.) vs двое друзей (gen.Plur.). Same meaning, different grammar.

fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Counting a group of people uses the collective numeral трое, followed by the genitive plural: трое студентов. Here студентов is already in the genitive plural, and that is exactly the form трое governs.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: There are two students on the team.
errorCorrection.explanation: Collective numerals (двое, трое, четверо) take the GENITIVE PLURAL, the same ending you use after пять: двое студентов. Студента is the genitive singular, which belongs after the ordinary number два (два студента), and that contrast is the whole point: два студента but двое студентов, same meaning, different grammar. After a collective numeral, always reach for the genitive plural.

Сутки ('a 24-hour day') exists only in the plural, and ordinary numbers cannot attach to a plural-only noun. You must use the collective трое: трое суток. Три is the ordinary cardinal, which сутки rejects.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: There are four men in the photo.
errorCorrection.explanation: After the collective numeral четверо the noun is in the genitive plural: четверо мужчин. Мужчины is the nominative plural or genitive singular, not the form a collective numeral governs. Even though мужчина ends in -а like a feminine noun, it is masculine and its genitive plural is мужчин, the form collective numerals require for a group of men.

minimalPairs.explanation: Counting children is the standard collective-numeral phrase: двое детей. Два is the ordinary number and is not used with дети in this everyday meaning; the collective двое is the natural choice.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Two pairs of scissors lie on the shelf.
minimalPairs.explanation: Ножницы exists only in the plural, so the ordinary две cannot attach to it. The collective numeral двое handles plural-only nouns: двое ножниц.

categorySorting.instruction: Decide which number to use: the ordinary number (два/три) or the collective (двое/трое).

reviewVocab.definition: collective numerals; count a group of people, children, and paired or plural-only nouns. Always take the genitive plural.
collective + genitive plural (двое детей) vs ordinary number + genitive singular (два друга). The noun ending tells you which number was used.
reviewVocab.example: Двое друзей пришли, а два других опоздали.

reviewVocab.definition: plural-only nouns; they cannot take the ordinary numbers, so you count them with collectives: двое суток, трое ножниц.
